set.body:
COUNTER-EVIDENCE BEAD. Four statistical claims tested by Monte Carlo. All hold, and the magnitudes recover planted ground truth rather than merely having the right sign. 3000 null replicates plus 800 signal replicates; about 7.5 minutes of compute.

CLAIM 1 - 'cross-products are unbiased around zero' (introduction.Rmd:126-127). Pure noise, no true effect, 20 features, 4 runs, n = 3000:

  estimator        mean        se        z
  signed        +0.00102   0.00285   +0.36
  coherent      -0.00085   0.00073   -1.16
  configuration +0.00180   0.00322   +0.56
  total         +0.00095   0.00332   +0.29

Every one within +/-1.2 standard errors of zero. The estimator is unbiased as claimed.

  NEGATIVES RETAINED: 52.4 percent of total estimates are below zero under the null.

That number is the whole argument for the package's negative-retention policy, expressed in one figure. An unbiased estimator centred at zero MUST be negative about half the time, so truncating at zero would bias every null voxel upward. This is the evidence that bd-01KZYARD5697TRN2Q3S0E153BM asked for - the missing 'why negative values are not a bug' vignette - and it is one line of simulation.

CLAIM 2 - 'coherent energy asks whether the local average reproduces' (intro:120-124). Planted a purely UNIVARIATE effect, every feature shifted identically by 1:

  coherent       1.0060        configuration  0.0131        ratio 77 : 1

Coherent recovers the planted magnitude - the contrast is a-b with a shifted by 1, so the squared effect is 1, and coherent reads 1.006.

CLAIM 3 - 'configuration energy asks whether spatial departures reproduce'. Planted a purely MULTIVARIATE effect, an exactly zero-mean +/-1 pattern:

  coherent       0.0008        configuration  1.0393        ratio 1339 : 1

Configuration recovers the pattern's mean square, which is 1, and coherent correctly reads essentially nothing.

So the decomposition is not merely an exact algebraic split - already verified separately as total = coherent + configuration to a difference of literally zero - it SEPARATES THE THING THE PROSE SAYS IT SEPARATES, and the two components read off the planted magnitudes on their respective sides.

CLAIM 4 - determinism. Identical seeds produce bitwise identical totals.

WHY THIS BEAD MATTERS FOR THE WORKSTREAM. Across four sweeps I have filed thirty-one findings, and a reader of this board could reasonably conclude the package is in trouble. It is not. The engine is unbiased, the decomposition is interpretable and recovers ground truth, six documented mathematical laws hold, the unification claim is true on both halves, and the estimator agrees with hand computation bitwise. Every defect I have filed is in the surface - names, messages, documentation, one seam, two silent behaviours.

DIRECT USE FOR THE DOCUMENTATION. Claims 1 through 3 are three short simulations that would make the most abstract part of the framework concrete: plant a univariate effect and watch coherent light up, plant a pattern and watch configuration light up, run the null and watch half the estimates go negative. That is the worked example the introduction is missing, and it writes itself from this bead.
set.title: Verified by simulation: unbiasedness holds and the coherent/configuration split means what the docs say
